t: This is the statue of Sidney Herbert, Lord Herbert of Lea, by the Irish sculptor J. H. Foley. It was put up by public subscription in 1867 and began life in the courtyard of Cumberland House on Pall Mall. It moved to Whitehall with the War Office, and then, eight years later, to Waterloo Place, where it stands beside the Crimean War Memorial. Here it is paired with a statue of Herbert's friend and fellow reformer Florence Nightingale. Herbert was a statesman and a close ally and confidant of Nightingale. Thomas Henry Wyatt is also credited with designing it.
